verdict_basis: 66.67% beats both baselines on raw accuracy, but ALL 5 errors are false positives on negative controls (0/5 specificity) -- 100% recall on genuine PII, 0% specificity on context-dependent non-PII text ('112', a git-verified test count, a room name, a port number, an agent's name). Checked with include_confidence=True whether a higher threshold fixes this: it does not -- false positive confidences (0.58-0.9999, e.g. '112' as phone number at 0.9999) overlap directly with true positive confidences (0.77-1.0), so no threshold value separates them. This is a genuine zero-shot entity-typing limitation (plausible entity type out of context, wrong in this context), not a scoring artifact or a tunable hyperparameter. Same class of over-eager-positive-bias failure found earlier today in CoherenceGate.
next_step_before_production: Not viable as a standalone confidence-threshold-gated filter. Would need either a larger held-out set to confirm this isn't sample noise (n=15 today), a fine-tuned/few-shot-calibrated label set, or pairing with a second-pass contextual check (e.g. the Sociedad SLM CoherenceGate reasoning approach) before touching any real PII-scrubbing path.
